context.title: Subarrays Distinct Element Sum of Squares I
context.problem: Given an integer array nums, return the sum of the squares of the number of distinct values in every nonempty contiguous subarray. Example: nums=[1,2,1] gives 15. Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

article.title: 🧠 Duplicates? Count Them Once! | Simple C++ + Visuals

sections.heading: 💡 The tiny trick
sections.markdown:
**A longer subarray doesn’t always have more distinct values.**

For `[1,2,1]`, adding the last `1` changes nothing in the set. The contribution stays `2² = 4`.

sections.heading: 🎯 Three moves
sections.markdown:
- Fix `i` and start with an empty set.
- Extend `j`, inserting `nums[j]`.
- Add `st.size()²` to `ans`.

sections.heading: Why it works
sections.markdown: **Why it works:** after each insert, `st` contains exactly the values in `nums[i..j]`; the loops visit every subarray once.

sections.heading: Remember this
sections.markdown: **Remember:** reset the set when the left boundary moves. Reuse it while the right boundary grows.

time.reason: n = nums.size(); O(n²) inserts, expected O(1) each. Hash collisions can degrade insertion; size() stays O(1).

space.reason: One set holds at most n distinct values.
